stem: Which of the following best describes the clinical definition of a birthmark according to the source material?

options.text: A skin lesion that must be present exactly at the moment of birth.
An imbalance or preponderance of specific skin components, such as melanocytes or blood vessels.
A temporary skin discoloration caused exclusively by birth trauma.
A growth consisting solely of overactive sweat glands and nerve fibers.

explanation: Birthmarks are explained as an excess or deficiency of normal skin tissues, such as the epidermis, dermis, or pigment cells.
rationale: Consider the structural composition of the skin and when these lesions typically appear.

optionExplanations.A: While the name implies presence at birth, many birthmarks only become visible or begin to grow in the first few weeks of life.
optionExplanations.B: Birthmarks are explained as an excess or deficiency of normal skin tissues, such as the epidermis, dermis, or pigment cells.
optionExplanations.C: Birthmarks are structural imbalances of skin components rather than bruising or trauma from the birthing process.
optionExplanations.D: The source lists various components like keratinocytes, melanocytes, and blood vessels, but does not describe birthmarks as being solely composed of sweat glands.

originalCorrectOptionTexts: An imbalance or preponderance of specific skin components, such as melanocytes or blood vessels.
